html:
André Matsoua was a Congolese activist from the Lari people near Brazzaville who founded a mutual aid society for Africans in Paris in 1926 and became, after his death, the messiah of a protest church.

A veteran of the French army, his Amicale collected money from Africans to fight for equal rights. The colonial authorities saw sedition, tried him in Brazzaville in 1930 and deported him. Riots followed. He died in prison in 1942.

Many followers refused to believe he was dead and refused taxes and voting in his name. Matsouanism became a religion and a voice of the Lari and the Pool region. Fulbert Youlou won their votes by presenting himself as heir to Matsoua, and the movement echoed the Kongo prophets such as Simon Kimbangu across the river in Belgian Congo.
